the-carnegie.mobility.1: The Carnegie is a handicap accessible venue, including handicap parking spots adjacent to the building, elevators to each level of the building, and a wheelchair ramp to the Eva G. Farris Education Center.
the-carnegie.mobility.2: Please note, the mezzanine level of the Otto M. Budig Theatre is not accessible via ramp or elevator.
the-carnegie.sensory.1: For select performances, The Carnegie is proud to offer fully accessible performances for the deaf and hard of hearing, featuring closed captioning and American Sign Language interpreters. For specific dates and availability, please contact The Carnegie Box Office at 859.957.1940.
the-carnegie.mobility.3: In addition to un-metered street parking on all four sides of our building, there are several surface lots available.
The Carnegie Parking Lot Located directly behind The Carnegie on the corner of Robbins and Greenup. Always open to patrons.
Unless otherwise specified, The Carnegie does not offer valet parking.
the-carnegie.sensory.2: Captioning has been offered for major theatrical performances at The Carnegie since 2006, thanks to the support of volunteers.
the-carnegie.mobility.5: Inside the original library building, two floors are connected by ornately carved dual winding staircases.
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati.mobility.1: Automatic doors from street into the theatre’s main entrance

Our elevator provides access between floors as well as to upper row accessible seating via the third-floor lobby entrance. Due to our historic buildings’ uneven floor heights, there are 4 stairs immediately before entering the theatre via the third-floor lobby; a wheelchair lift provides access to this height difference for patrons using mobility devices.
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati.sensory.2: We provide large-print and braille programs for every production along with audio-described performances on select dates throughout the season.
One audio-described performance is offered for each regular-season production; these are indicated on our filterable event listings page.
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati.cognitive.1: Relaxed performances feature accommodations including lower sound levels, lower light levels, reduction of strobe lighting, freedom to talk and move around during the show, and more.
Patrons attending relaxed performances can access pre-visit guides, social narratives, and other resources to prepare for their trip.
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati.mobility.3: Additional parking for those with disabilities available at 12th and Vine surface lot and the Gateway Garage.
Wheelchair-level ticket counter at box office
ensemble-theatre-cincinnati.sensory.3: Additionally, fidgets, noise-canceling headphones, sunglasses, and snacks are available in the lobby anytime.
We offer assistive listening devices for all performances as well as ASL-interpreted performances on select dates throughout the season.
You may also dial 711 to connect to our box office via Ohio Relay services
memorial-hall-otr.mobility.1: The basement, first and second floors of Memorial Hall are fully accessible via the patron elevator on the north side of the building (the right side of the building when facing the front entrance), which may be entered on the street level.
memorial-hall-otr.mobility.2: In addition, the Annie W. and Elizabeth M. Anderson Theater is equipped with a number of wheelchair/scooter-accessible seating locations. For additional information on accessible seating, please contact the Box Office at (513) 977.8838.
